items.item: Every status column heading shows the status name and its ticket count, and the count equals the cards shown or the column states how many are not shown (such as "Showing 20 of 134")
items.evidence: renderBoard() header: ''+s.label+''+countText+''; countText = items.length (or 'items.length / limit', or 'items.length of countAll' when filtered). Screenshot shows 'Open 6', 'In progress 7 / 8', 'Waiting on customer 7 / 5 · Over limit' matching the number of cards rendered in each column.

items.item: Each card shows the ticket number (such as #4821), subject, customer, priority as a word or code (such as "P1 · Urgent") and the assignee, or an explicit "Unassigned"
items.evidence:
cardHtml(t): code span 'TCK-1041', subject button, customer

, badge(PRIORITIES[t.priority].label,...) e.g. 'High', and assigneeHtml which renders avatar+name or 'Unassigned' — visible on every card in first.png (e.g. TCK-1041 'Unassigned', TCK-1042 'MC Maria Chen').

items.item: Open tickets show the time left to the next SLA target and which target it is (such as "Resolution due in 2h 15m"), and breached tickets show how long they are overdue (such as "Breached 40m ago") in text or with an icon, not by colour alone
items.evidence: getUrgency() only ever produces generic 'Due in ' + duration or 'Overdue ' + duration (e.g. 'Due in 2h', 'Overdue 1 day' in first.png) — there is only one undifferentiated dueAt per ticket and the text never names which SLA target it refers to (e.g. first response vs resolution), so the 'which target' requirement is not met even though overdue duration text is shown.

items.item: Tickets in a waiting status (such as "Waiting on customer") show their SLA timer as paused instead of counting down
items.evidence: getUrgency(t) has no branch for t.status === 'waiting'; it computes the same countdown/overdue text as open tickets. TCK-1031 and TCK-1039 (status 'waiting') show 'Due 11/07/2026, 8:00 PM' and 'Overdue 1 day' exactly like open-column cards — no 'Paused' label or icon anywhere in cardHtml/panelBodyHtml.

items.item: Within each column the cards are ordered by SLA due time or by priority, and the board states which ordering is used
items.evidence: sortWithinColumn(list) sorts by PRIORITIES[...].order then dueAt.getTime(), so ordering is implemented, but no text or label anywhere in the markup (column header, toolbar, or elsewhere) tells the user which ordering is applied.

items.item: Search finds tickets by number, subject or customer, and filters cover assignee (including "Me" and "Unassigned"), priority and SLA state (such as breached or due within 1 hour)
items.evidence: matchesFilters() checks t.code/t.subject/t.customer for search, #filter-assignee (incl. '__unassigned__' option) plus a separate #filter-mine 'Assigned to me' button, and #filter-priority — but there is no SLA-state filter control anywhere (#filter-assignee, #filter-priority, #filter-type are the only selects); breached/due-within-1h cannot be filtered.

items.item: Each card has keyboard-reachable actions to assign the ticket (including "Assign to me") and to change its status without dragging, with accessible names that include the ticket number
items.evidence:
Status change exists via a focusable kebab button aria-label="Actions for ticket "+t.code opening a 'Move to…' menu (data-move-ticket) — satisfies the status half. But there is no assign control anywhere: the panel only renders assignee as static text ('

Assignee

'+t.assignee+'

') with no button/select, and no 'Assign to me' action exists on the card or panel.

items.item: An empty column shows a short message instead of blank space, a search or filter with no matches offers to clear it, and loading and failed-load (with retry) states exist
items.evidence:
Empty column: '

No tickets in '+s.label.toLowerCase()+'

'. No-match board state: 'No tickets match these filters' + #board-clear-filters button calling clearAllFilters(). Loading: showSkeleton() renders animated skeleton columns. Failed load: #error-state with message "Couldn't load tickets..." and #retry-btn wired to retry logic.

items.item: Every relative time (such as "Updated 3h ago") also exposes the exact date, time and timezone, in a <time datetime> element or a title attribute
items.evidence: #updated-stamp renders plain text "Updated just now" with no <time> element or title attribute. Also in cardHtml, urgent/breached SLA text (badge tone set, e.g. 'Overdue 2h', 'Due in 1h') is emitted via badge() as plain text with no datetime/title — only the non-urgent branch ('tone' null) wraps text in '<time datetime=...>'. The most important relative times (breached/soon-due) expose no exact timestamp.

notes: No template tells were found: no greeting header, no KPI tiles, no gradients/glass/backdrop-blur, no uppercase tracked labels, no emoji icons (SVGs used throughout), no rainbow status colors (muted slate/blue/amber/green/red mapped sensibly by tone), no sidebar (so no promo card or navy/indigo sidebar), no decorative chart, no card-in-card nesting, no hover-lift transforms, and radii are standard (4/6px, not oversized). Avatars (e.g. 'MC', 'JO') are initials for real named agents/users, a legitimate use, not an initials-avatar-non-person tell. The page is a well-built, non-templated-looking build; its checklist failures are functional gaps (no assign action, no SLA-state filter, no waiting-status pause, unstated sort order, undifferentiated SLA target naming, missing exact-timestamp exposure for urgent SLA text) rather than cosmetic AI-template markers.
